title: Are Your Greatest Weaknesses Also Your Greatest Strengths?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note challenges the tidy cliche that a leader's greatest strength is also their greatest weakness by asking whether the reverse holds true as well. The piece argues that overused strengths curdle into liabilities, but also that traits typically labeled as flaws (risk aversion, perfectionism, fear of failure, disorganization) can become genuine assets in the right context. The author reframes weakness-management not as elimination but as calibrated exposure: leaders grow by repeatedly practicing in the very situations their weaknesses make uncomfortable, rather than avoiding them. Avoidance is identified as the real mechanism that hardens a weakness into a permanent limitation. The piece closes by urging leaders to treat weaknesses as an "accent" to manage rather than a flaw to eliminate.
points: Weaknesses are not fixed liabilities; risk aversion, perfectionism, fear of failure, and disorganization each have contexts in which they function as assets.
Avoidance, not the trait itself, is what turns a weakness into a dysfunction — leaders who dodge feedback or public speaking amplify those very weaknesses over time.
Growth comes from repeated, incremental exposure to the exact situations a weakness makes uncomfortable, not from trying to eliminate the trait outright.
The healthiest leadership posture treats a weakness as an accent to be managed rather than a flaw to be erased.
quotes: An aversion to risks can provide much needed caution in a life-threatening event.
When we let our strengths grab ahold of us without being checked, they become a weakness.
Most weaknesses become dysfunctional precisely because we avoid the situations that allow us to conquer them.
The weakness of taking feedback poorly becomes amplified the more we shun criticism.
The best leaders work on their weaknesses by applying them. Let's face it. Most weaknesses never disappear entirely.
We don't overcome weakness nearly as much as we commit to making them more productive.
